paper.title_en: NGC 1300: A rich reservoir of ultraluminous X-ray sources
paper.abstract_en: We present the first systematic multi-epoch study of the X-ray source population of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300, using 12 archival Chandra observations spanning more than 15 years and archival Swift/XRT monitoring. Within the optical extent of the galaxy, we identify 42 X-ray sources, including six ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) and 13 ULX candidates. The candidates have measured luminosities below $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, but their upper uncertainty bounds reach or exceed this threshold in at least one epoch. We examine source luminosities, long-term variability, broad-band spectral properties, and epoch-resolved X-ray luminosity functions (XLFs). Ten sources meet our transient criterion, seven have a variability significance of $S_{\rm var}\geq3$, and four meet both criteria. X32 is a highly variable ULX with a peak X-ray luminosity of $1.5\times10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$, more than 715 times the non-detection upper limit. The hardness-intensity diagrams show diverse spectral behavior among the luminous sources, with no common hardness-luminosity evolution. X32 remains predominantly hard despite its large luminosity variations, and its X-ray colors are consistent with the empirical high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) region of the color-color diagram. The cumulative XLFs above $10^{38}$ erg s$^{-1}$ have slopes of $β\simeq0.6$ to $1.0$, with evidence for a broken power law in only a few epochs. The number of off-nuclear sources reaching $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ranges from zero to four per epoch. Long-term source variability thus strongly shapes the bright end of the XLF and makes the observed ULX census of NGC 1300 strongly epoch dependent. Multi-epoch monitoring is essential for establishing representative ULX populations in nearby galaxies.
